title: Measure forge-listed SSH keys among pgpkeys holders
description: Idea (2026-10-23): forges publish keys (GitHub <user>.keys/.gpg and /users/<u>/ssh_signing_keys; GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, sourcehut equivalents). Could feed a separate small tool that suggests ssh-* lines in a holder's unsigned migrate draft, marked forge-sourced. Never proof: forge data grants no tier, is not continuity, never enters the registry unsigned (would add a forge as a trust root). MEASURE FIRST: of pgpkeys holders at the freeze commit, how many have a forge account whose published GPG keys include the same fingerprint (the only clean link), and how many of those list an SSH signing key (and how many sk-). Catch: GitHub has no lookup by GPG fingerprint, so candidate accounts must come from emails (commit-search API, rate-limited) and then be confirmed by fingerprint. Real names/emails stay local; commit only aggregates. Decide on the tool from the numbers.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate counts (holders, fingerprint-matched forge accounts, with SSH signing key, with sk- key) with method and date recorded in bead notes; no personal data committed; go/no-go recommendation for the suggestion tool.
